stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the profile of Jackson Pollock in Life magazine, August 1949, which asked whether he was the greatest living painter in the United States. Pollock painted by splattering, pouring, and dripping paint onto large canvases laid on the floor. His work showed no recognizable people, places, or objects.

stem: Abstract expressionism, centered in New York City, best reflects which broader change in postwar American culture?

options.text: American artists broke from European styles and set their own course
American painters returned to realistic scenes of farm life
options.misconception: Background from the books: abstract painters left realistic scenes behind, so they did not return to them.

options.text: The government banned modern art from public museums
options.misconception: Background from the books: no ban on modern art existed, and Pollock's fame came from magazines and museums.

options.text: Most Americans came to agree on what good painting should look like
options.misconception: Background from the books: Life had to ask whether Pollock was great, which shows Americans disagreed about his art.

rationales.A: Background from the books: abstract expressionism, centered in New York, made American art a world force instead of a follower of Europe.
rationales.B: Background from the books: abstract painters left realistic scenes behind, so they did not return to them.
rationales.C: Background from the books: no ban on modern art existed, and Pollock's fame came from magazines and museums.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Life had to ask whether Pollock was great, which shows Americans disagreed about his art.
rationales.general:
1. Background from the books: before the war, American painters mostly followed European styles.
2. Background from the books: after the war, a New York movement put process and feeling first, in a style no European school had made.
3. When a country's artists stop following and start leading, its culture has come of age.
Remember: A new style centered at home marks a culture finding its own voice.
